# Plan: Task Fidelity — Collection-Shaped Answers, End to End

## 1. Overview

Waves 1–2 and their gap closure hardened the interaction layer (filling, clicking, widget recovery, obstruction). Run `20260925T130634Z-research-e1fd1b9d` never touched that layer. The user asked:

> I want to check the top offers and lowest price for a brand new 2026 hyundai santa fe calligraphy trim in AWD near me. List dealer name, their lowest price, color (exterior and interior). Use autotrader.com

They received a price range, one dealer name lifted from a search-engine snippet, and no colors from the site they named. The run took 6.9 minutes, 15 turns and 48 Chrome launches, and half of its 22 searches failed. The published Brief:

- told the user that the site "renders each listing's dealer name and exterior/interior colors client-side". That claim is false: our extractor discarded fields the page served (G2).
- was titled "…AWD offers" although no AWD filter was ever applied or checked.
- carried six findings, every one uncited (`editorial: true`).
- listed 17 sources, including used-car inventory pages, a salvage-auction VIN page, and reviews.
- reported no notices about the 11 failed searches or the exhausted navigation budget.

The identical goal ran on 2026-09-19 (`20260919T231319Z-research-86e1054e`), with the same model and the same prompt version `agent-v8`. That run finished in 2.6 minutes with four named dealers, prices, and colors, but only by silently ignoring "Use autotrader.com". The two runs took opposite strategies and reported two different "lowest prices" ($46,214 vs $43,204). **Neither delivered what the user expected: a table of Autotrader listings with dealer, price, and colors.**

**The finding.** Yantra's evidence pipeline is _article-shaped_: search returns articles, Readability extracts articles, results carry no links, and the Brief is prose plus bullets. This task is _collection-shaped_, and so are most real-world tasks (shopping, rentals, jobs, travel, events, local services). A collection task means filtering a listing, reading repeated records, following records to detail pages, and returning one sourced row per item. Every layer of the pipeline failed the collection shape in its own way, and none of those failures is site-specific. The model diagnosed its predicament correctly: 14 of its 15 turns reasoned about listing links and detail pages it had no way to reach. The tools, not the model, were the bottleneck.

**What worked, and must not regress.** The explicit location grant reached the model ("user location: frisco, texas"), so nothing was inferred from the timezone. The agent respected the trust boundary for 14 turns, inventing no listing IDs and no API parameters. It disclosed that it could not complete the table. Publication succeeded after budget exhaustion (the terminal exemption works). Third-party PII stayed redacted.

**What this plan is not.** It does not revisit the interaction layer (FEAT-031–040), browser management (FEAT-041–047), or the deterministic `--no-llm` synthesizer. It adds no site-specific logic: every new signal is structural (repeated DOM records, schema.org data, link structure, response shape), and every fixture encodes a nameable generic pattern.

### G1 — `research` cannot open the site the user named (FEAT-052)

The research profile registers `web_search`, `web_fetch`, `script_run`, `result_publish`, and `workflow_run` — no browser tool ([`profiles.ts:66-78`](../packages/agent/src/runtime/profiles.ts#L66-L78)). Browsing exists only behind `YANTRA_AGENT_RESEARCH_BROWSE=1` ([`profiles.ts:185-198`](../packages/agent/src/runtime/profiles.ts#L185-L198)). That is an undocumented environment variable, the "remember a mode flag" pattern memory forbids, and it grants only navigate/observe/extract even when set. The per-run prompt meanwhile states "Scope: browser and web work only." unconditionally ([`prompt.ts:150`](../packages/agent/src/runtime/prompt.ts#L150)).

[`docs/usage.md:390-392`](../docs/usage.md#L390-L392) routes "browse or act on a website" to `do` and "investigate a broad topic" to `research`. A user researching a car purchase reasonably picks `research`. Nothing told them that a goal naming a site and asking for listing-level fields cannot be met by that command.

### G2 — An article extractor on a collection page (FEAT-051)

`web_fetch` of the Frisco results page returned 2,302 bytes. The text was facet labels ("Elantra (238) … Calligraphy (44) …") followed by bare price blocks ("50,265 / MSRP$50,255 / Dealer Fees Included"). The card prices survived; the card titles and seller names in the same cards did not. The fields were in the page: DuckDuckGo's snippet for a sibling results URL of the same template reads "AutoNation Hyundai North Richland Hills 27.02 mi. away … New 2026 Hyundai Santa Fe Calligraphy 3 mi 50,230 MSRP $50,220".

[`ReadabilityExtractor`](../packages/core/src/extraction/readability.ts#L17-L61) pre-removes `nav`, `aside`, and `form`, then runs Mozilla Readability. Readability is built to keep article prose and discard link-dense repeated blocks, which is exactly where a collection keeps its records. The browser path is no better:

- `browser_extract` `content` is `document.body.innerText` collapsed onto one line ([`agent-controller.ts:1141-1144`](../packages/core/src/browser/agent-controller.ts#L1141-L1144)).
- `browser_extract` `table` reads only the first `<table>` ([`agent-controller.ts:1146-1157`](../packages/core/src/browser/agent-controller.ts#L1146-L1157); TODO line 214).
- No path reads schema.org structured data; JSON-LD is parsed only for `datePublished` ([`readability.ts:112-127`](../packages/core/src/extraction/readability.ts#L112-L127)).

**The second-order cost:** the agent could not see why the fields were missing, so it invented an explanation ("renders client-side") and published it as fact. An extractor that does not report its own coverage turns a tool gap into a false claim about the world.

### G3 — No links, so nothing beyond search results is reachable (FEAT-051)

`web_fetch` tells the model to fetch "a link discovered inside previously fetched content" ([`web-fetch.ts:51-52`](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/web-fetch.ts#L51-L52)), but its result contains no links ([`web-fetch.ts:192-202`](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/web-fetch.ts#L192-L202)). The system prompt correctly forbids inventing path segments, parameter names, or identifiers ([`prompt.ts:35`](../packages/agent/src/runtime/prompt.ts#L35)).

Together, those two facts make pagination, facet filters (AWD), and detail pages (colors) unreachable by construction. The agent spent 12 searches trying to make a search engine surface detail URLs (`inurl:vehicledetails`, `"vehicledetails.xhtml"`, VIN-prefix queries). TODO line 208 left the provenance question open. The missing design is links harvested from a fetched page and attested by that page.

### G4 — Half the searches failed, and the cause was thrown away (FEAT-048, FEAT-050)

11 of 22 `web_search` calls returned `SEARCH_FAILED` within 1.4–1.9 s. The model issued searches in concurrent pairs. All 11 failures fell inside those 10 pairs, only one pair fully succeeded, and both solo searches succeeded. That pattern is consistent with the provider throttling concurrent scrapes, but it cannot be confirmed, because the cause was discarded.

The provider was DuckDuckGo HTML scraped through headless Chrome, auto-selected because no keyed provider is configured. `DuckDuckGoSearchProvider` throws typed, actionable errors: `anomaly-challenge` ("configure a keyed search provider") and `empty-results` ([`duckduckgo.ts:49-63`](../packages/core/src/extraction/search/duckduckgo.ts#L49-L63)). `web_search` discards both in a bare `catch {}` and substitutes "temporarily unavailable", `retryable: true` ([`web-search.ts:132-141`](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/web-search.ts#L132-L141)). `runtime.jsonl` holds 121 lines, every one at info level, with zero warnings. The model was told the failure was retryable and responded with more concurrent searches. Memory → Coding Standards: "Never silently swallow errors."

`resolveProvider` builds a new provider on every call ([`orchestrator.ts:1340-1349`](../packages/agent/src/runtime/orchestrator.ts#L1340-L1349); "selected search provider" logged 22 times), so no object exists that could hold a per-run gate or breaker. The 2026-09-19 run issued the same parallel pattern with zero failures. Blocking depends on time and IP reputation, which is why politeness must be structural rather than tuned.

### G5 — The same page fetched seven times; 48 Chrome launches (FEAT-050)

| URL (Autotrader results pages)                 | Fetches |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `…/new-cars/2026/hyundai/santa-fe/calligraphy` | 7       |
| `…/new-cars/2026/hyundai/santa-fe`             | 3       |
| `…/new-cars/2026/hyundai/santa-fe/dallas-tx`   | 2       |

The run's 30 navigations split into 17 distinct pages read, 9 re-fetches of pages already read, and 4 failed fetches ([`url-policy.ts:185`](../packages/agent/src/runtime/url-policy.ts#L185) charges each). Tool results totalled 103 KB, much of it the same facet text resent.

Every SERP scrape launches a Chrome ([`scrape-transport.ts:77-80`](../packages/core/src/extraction/search/scrape-transport.ts#L77-L80)), and every escalated page fetch launches another ([`fetcher.ts:137-140`](../packages/core/src/extraction/fetcher.ts#L137-L140)). `BrowserFallbackFetcher` ignores its timeout and abort signal (`_opts`) and waits for `networkidle2` ([`fetcher.ts:132-144`](../packages/core/src/extraction/fetcher.ts#L132-L144)). The run already owns a browser through `AgentBrowserController` ([`orchestrator.ts:1315`](../packages/agent/src/runtime/orchestrator.ts#L1315)) that the fetch path never uses. `web_search` also always inline-fetches at least one hit, because `limit` has a minimum of 1 ([`web-search.ts:55-61`](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/web-search.ts#L55-L61)), so a cheap discovery query does not exist.

### G6 — Our own budget exhaustion recorded as the site's fault (FEAT-048)

The 30-navigation budget ran out inside a search. The per-URL gate maps every URL-policy rejection to `{reason: 'blocklist'}` ([`web-search.ts:195-199`](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/web-search.ts#L195-L199)). That becomes failure stage `blocked`, which `rankReasonForFailureStage` turns into a negative `blocked` rank signal ([`ranking/recording.ts:15-26`](../packages/core/src/ranking/recording.ts#L15-L26)). Autotrader and Hyundai's own site were penalized in cross-run ranking because of a limit we imposed.

The agent learned of the exhaustion only from a per-site line reading "blocked — blocklist - url-policy: Navigation budget of 30 navigations is exhausted". It never saw a running meter and had no way to know that each search costs up to three navigations.

### G7 — The output contract cannot hold the answer (FEAT-053)

- The protocol Brief already has `sections` and `facets.comparison` ([`brief.ts:108-149`](../packages/protocol/src/schemas/brief.ts#L108-L149)), and both renderers draw them ([`to-markdown.ts:67-74`](../packages/core/src/brief/to-markdown.ts#L67-L74), [`to-html.ts:94-101`](../packages/core/src/brief/to-html.ts#L94-L101)). But `buildBriefFromAgentContent` passes only title, overview, key_findings, and sources ([`result-publish.ts:481-511`](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/result-publish.ts#L481-L511)). A table is structurally unreachable from an agentic run.
- `withLedgerEvidence` coerces every finding to uncited editorial text because model citation numbers are numbered per call ([`result-publish.ts:219-231`](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/result-publish.ts#L219-L231)). Every agentic Brief therefore bypasses the protocol's "no uncited claims" guarantee ([`brief.ts:10-13`](../packages/protocol/src/schemas/brief.ts#L10-L13)).
- The source list is every page touched, not the pages that support a claim.
- `notices` is empty and `metadata.search_provider` is `null`, although the runtime knew the facts for both.

### G8 — The audit log is corrupted by its own sanitizer (FEAT-048)

All 13 successful `web_search`/`web_fetch` end records in `tool-calls.jsonl` hold an `output_sanitized` that is not valid JSON. The Pi seam serializes the payload, runs the text sanitizer over it, then re-parses ([`event-map.ts:58-68`](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/event-map.ts#L58-L68)).

`URL_IN_TEXT_RE = /https?:\/\/[^\s"'<>]+/gi` ([`strippers.ts:46`](../packages/core/src/sanitizer/strippers.ts#L46)) excludes `"` but not `\`. Inside the double-encoded `content[].text`, it therefore captures `…/dallas-tx\`. `new URL()` ([`strippers.ts:457`](../packages/core/src/sanitizer/strippers.ts#L457)) normalizes that backslash to `/`, which un-escapes the closing quote. The re-parse fails and the broken text is stored. Stored URLs gain trailing slashes (`…/posts/10160610212631779//`), and each false rewrite counts as a sanitizer hit.

The model-visible copy was correct. The stable audit projection, the artifact memory designates as "the durable observability artifact", is the copy that is wrong. Its readers ([`report-builder.ts:74`](../packages/core/src/audit/report-builder.ts#L74), [`delta-cost.ts:77`](../packages/core/src/audit/delta-cost.ts#L77)) silently lose the details. This analysis had to be done from the raw provider session log instead.

### G9 — No explicit goal contract, and the guidance conflicts (FEAT-052)

The model received four instructions that pull against each other:

- The research addendum: "Research broadly … use independent sources" ([`profiles.ts:71`](../packages/agent/src/runtime/profiles.ts#L71)).
- The user: "Use autotrader.com".
- Every search result: "do not search again for the same topic" ([`web-search.ts:284-287`](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/web-search.ts#L284-L287)).
- The system prompt: "at most one materially different fallback" ([`prompt.ts:41`](../packages/agent/src/runtime/prompt.ts#L41)).

The user's filters, required fields, and required source existed only in free text, so neither the model nor the runtime could check the delivery against them. On 2026-09-19 the run substituted sources silently. On 2026-09-25 it honored the source, lost the deliverable, and asserted an unverified filter in the title.

Separately, the prompt's "tool retries: 3" ([`prompt.ts:141`](../packages/agent/src/runtime/prompt.ts#L141)) actually describes a consecutive-identical-failure breaker ([`orchestrator.ts:771-794`](../packages/agent/src/runtime/orchestrator.ts#L771-L794)), not a retry policy. Because successes and failures alternated across the parallel pairs, the breaker never tripped.

### G10 — A 200 response can be a challenge page (FEAT-050)

During this analysis, one plain GET of the Frisco results URL returned HTTP 200 with a 3.7 KB interstitial: a CAPTCHA-widget form and "the site is currently unavailable". `shouldEscalateToBrowser` ([`fetcher.ts:224-238`](../packages/core/src/extraction/fetcher.ts#L224-L238)) sends a page like that to Chrome only because it happens to be under 10 KB, has a script `src`, and has no `<article>`/`<main>`. A challenge page with a `<main>` element, or one over 10 KB, would be extracted as content and published as a source. Outside the DuckDuckGo SERP parser, nothing classifies a response as a challenge, so memory's "honor bot detection; hand off" rule is currently enforced by accident.

### G11 — Smaller gaps, corroborated

- `usage.json` shows `calls: []` and zero totals, while the manifest's agent block reports 15 turns and $0.165. This reproduces TODO line 272.
- The goal recorded by two earlier runs reads "top 5 hybrid SUVs to buy now for under ,000". The shell expanded `$40` before Yantra saw the goal. Nothing echoes the received goal, so the user cannot notice.
- Dealer phone numbers arrive as `[redacted-phone]`. For business listings, that contact data matters to the user. This is a privacy-policy question and is deferred (§12).

## 6. Security Considerations

> Standing rules are in [`memory.md`](./memory.md) → Security. Five concerns are specific to this plan.

### FEAT-051: discovered links turn page content into navigation authority

A harvested link is page-authored, and a prompt-injected page can plant links.

- A discovered link is navigable only through the existing URL policy: length cap, https, credential-shape scan, host budget, and ethics gate. Provenance answers "where did this URL come from?" and relaxes nothing else.
- Provenance records the containing source (`S3`), and the audit records each hop, so an exfiltration attempt is visible as a chain.
- Links are bounded per page (at most 40), deduplicated, and ranked same-site first. `javascript:`, `data:`, and fragment-only links are dropped.
- Hand-assembled URLs remain refused. This closes the laundering path TODO line 208 describes instead of widening it.

### FEAT-051: structured data is untrusted input

JSON-LD is page-authored. It is parsed as data and never evaluated, bounded by bytes and depth, filtered by a schema.org `@type` allowlist, and every string passes the same sanitizer profile as page text.

### FEAT-052: browsing inside `research`

Research browsing is read-only: navigate, observe, and extract, with no click and no fill. Research therefore never submits, purchases, or authenticates. The ephemeral profile, ethics gate, and host budgets are unchanged. A goal that needs interaction ends in a precise handoff to `yantra do`, never an in-run escalation.

### FEAT-050: challenge pages and search politeness

- A challenge seen **in the browser** is terminal for that URL. It produces a `blocked` failure, a Brief notice, and a handoff. It is never extracted, never retried in a loop, and never "solved".
- Serializing a scraped search provider, and stopping it after a challenge, is how the run honors that provider's rate limiting. There is no UA rotation, proxying, or fingerprint change.
- Whether an HTTP-tier challenge on the honest `YantraBot` UA may fall back to one browser render is a policy decision (§12, item 4). Whichever way it is decided, the code must make the decision explicit and audit it.

### FEAT-048: the audit sanitization fix must not weaken redaction

Structural sanitization (walking string leaves, recursing into JSON-in-string leaves) must apply the same profile to every leaf. A property test asserts both halves: the output re-parses, and canary secrets and PII are still redacted.

## 7. Architecture & Design (Plan-Specific)

### Two shapes of evidence

```text
response ─► classify ─┬─ challenge ──► blocked failure + notice + handoff (never extracted)
                      ├─ error page ─► fetch failure
                      ├─ js shell ───► render in the shared browser, classify again
                      └─ content ────► page shape ─┬─ article    ─► readable text (today's path, unchanged)
                                                   ├─ collection ─► records + links + structured entities
                                                   ├─ table      ─► all tables
                                                   └─ detail     ─► label/value pairs + structured entities
                                   ─► evidence ledger (S3, S3#r5) ─► contract-aware publish ─► table/sections, cited by ID
```

Article pages keep today's Readability output byte-for-byte, so existing research quality and the deterministic pipeline are unaffected. The shape decision reuses the single DOM parse the extractor already performs (memory → Architecture: diagnostic work paid only where needed).

### Collection extraction, stated so it cannot become site logic

1. Find containers whose children form at least three siblings with similar structural signatures (tag path, depth, child-tag multiset), each holding a link and non-trivial text.
2. Score each container by record count, text richness, link presence, and numeric-token presence. Penalize candidates inside `nav`/`header`/`footer`/`aside` landmarks. A sibling list whose items are short labels with parenthesized counts linking to variants of the current URL is a **facet list**: it yields `facet` links, not records.
3. For each record, emit: primary link, title (first heading or anchor text), ordered text segments, label/value pairs (`dt`/`dd`, in-record `th`/`td`, "Label: value" text), and numeric tokens tagged by kind (currency, distance, count).
4. Bound the output (at most 25 records per page, 400 characters per record, overflow counted) and state coverage: records found, fields per record, what was dropped.

No step consults a host, URL, or class name. Schema.org entities complement records. They are generic vocabulary (`Product`, `Offer`, `ItemList`, `Organization`, `Place`, `Event`, and their subtypes) with every scalar property kept up to a byte cap. Nothing special-cases one vertical's properties.

### Evidence identity has one owner

The run document cache (FEAT-050) mints `S<n>` on the first ingestion of a normalized URL. FEAT-051 adds record anchors `S<n>#r<k>`. Tools keep taking URLs as input, so no new indirection is introduced. The publisher (FEAT-053) maps cited IDs onto protocol `sources[].n`. This resolves the per-call numbering problem that forced `withLedgerEvidence` to strip every citation. The fix is a run-wide ID shown in every result, not a smarter guess at publish time.

### The goal contract

- The agent declares the contract early through `task_contract`. It is **not** a precondition for evidence tools, so small models cannot stall on it. When a contract exists, the publisher validates `fulfillment` against it. When a `research`/`do` run declares none, the run gets a notice.
- The runtime uses the contract three ways. `required_sources` drives a per-row and per-finding host check: off-contract rows move to a labeled "alternatives" section and are never merged into the answer. `required_fields` drives coverage per table row: an empty cell must say "not shown on source". `filters` must each appear in `constraints[]` with a status, and unverified or violated constraints produce notices and render under the title.
- Attended runs echo the contract to stderr ("Understood: a table of … from autotrader.com; filters …"). A misreading is visible in the first seconds instead of in the Brief.

### Run-scoped acquisition services

Core provides three services: a `SearchService` (provider resolved once, politeness gate, challenge breaker), a `DocumentStore` (normalized-URL cache, ID minting, navigation charged per real network fetch), and a `PagePool` (one lazily launched browser per run, a fresh isolated context per fetch, bounded concurrency, timeout and abort honored). The orchestrator constructs one of each per run and injects them through `RunServices` ([`orchestrator.ts:1287-1367`](../packages/agent/src/runtime/orchestrator.ts#L1287-L1367)). The deterministic `research --no-llm` and `ask` loops keep their current fetch/extract wiring in this plan; adopting the services there is deferred.

### Why `research` gets read-only browsing, not clicks

On server-rendered collections, navigating discovered links covers pagination, facet links, and detail pages, which is the majority case. "Load more" buttons and script-only filters belong to `do`, which has the confirmation gateway. The harness counts `INTERACTION_REQUIRED` handoffs, and clicks in research are reconsidered only on that evidence.

### Target trace for this run's goal (what "fixed" looks like)

1. `task_contract`: deliverable table; fields dealer, price, exterior color, interior color; filters new, 2026, Santa Fe, Calligraphy, AWD, near Frisco TX; required source autotrader.com; ranking price ascending; top 5–10.
2. `web_search` with `limit: 0` to discover the results-page URL. No navigation is charged.
3. `web_fetch` of the results page returns shape `collection`: records (title, price, MSRP, seller, distance, link), facet and pagination links, and any structured entities.
4. Follow a drivetrain facet link if the page exposes one. Otherwise, verify drivetrain per row on detail pages.
5. `web_fetch` the top detail links (the cache prevents repeats). Each returns shape `detail`, with label/value pairs including the colors.
6. `result_publish` a table whose rows cite `S5#r1`, `S7`, …, with constraints (AWD verified per row), fulfillment, and notices for any gaps.

Expected cost: 8–12 navigations, 6–8 turns, under 4 minutes. If the browser meets a challenge on the required source, the run reports `blocked` with a handoff, and other sources appear only as labeled alternatives.

### Sequencing

- **FEAT-048 first.** It is small, and it fixes defects that corrupt the evidence every later feature is measured by: unparseable audit records, swallowed causes, and rank penalties. This is the same argument that put obstruction first in Wave 2.
- **FEAT-049 second.** Baseline the current pipeline on outcome-level scenarios before changing it. Two anecdotal runs of one goal already disagree. Without a harness, every later improvement is another anecdote.
- **FEAT-050 and FEAT-051 next, in parallel.** Acquisition owns evidence identity and the shared browser; extraction consumes both.
- **FEAT-052 then.** Turning on research browsing is worth it only once extraction can read collections and offer links.
- **FEAT-053 last.** It consumes IDs (050/051), the contract (052), and run facts (048).

## 8. Coding Standards (Plan-Specific Overrides)

**No overrides — see memory.** These rules are load-bearing here:

- _Never write website-specific logic._ Page shape, record detection, link kinds, and challenge classification are structural. The challenge vocabulary is a short, documented list of standard challenge-widget markers. These are cross-site components in the same category as ARIA roles, not a site list. The list carries a comment justifying it under this rule.
- _Never silently swallow errors._ G4 is a direct violation. FEAT-048 adds a boundary test that forbids an untyped `catch {}` on a tool's `run` path unless it maps to a stable code or logs.
- _Advice may only name an engineered move._ "Follow a link from `links[]`" is legal only when the result contains links. `SEARCH_BLOCKED` advises navigating to a URL already in the results, or publishing; both moves exist.
- _A tool result says what happened._ Extraction results state their own shape and coverage, so the agent never has to guess why data is missing. G2's false "client-side" claim is the failure this rule prevents.
- _Diagnostic work is paid only where needed._ Shape classification and record detection reuse the existing parse. Challenge classification reads the response already in hand. Assert both with call counts.

## 9. Testing Strategy (Plan-Specific)

- **FEAT-049 fixture sites**, each a nameable generic pattern served by the loopback e2e host. Site names may appear only as provenance in header comments.
  - `faceted-listing`: server-rendered repeated cards (title, price, seller line, distance, link), facet links, pagination links, and detail pages with attribute tables. Some items fail a filter, so constraint verification matters.
  - `structured-listing`: the same data exposed only through schema.org JSON-LD.
  - `client-rendered-listing`: records injected by script after load.
  - `challenge-interstitial`: HTTP 200 with a CAPTCHA-widget form. Must be reported as blocked, never extracted.
  - `article`: long-form prose. This guards against Readability regressions.
  - `multi-table`: the answer is in the second table (closes TODO line 214).
- **A scripted search provider**, test-only and injected through the existing provider seam, returns deterministic SERPs pointing at the fixtures. Fault modes: challenge-on-concurrency, empty, and timeout.
- **The deterministic tier gates CI** (`@no-llm`, all three OSes). Per fixture it asserts shape, record count and fields, link kinds and provenance, structured entities, challenge classification, cache hits and network-fetch counts, evidence IDs, notices, and that the audit JSON re-parses.
- **The agentic tier runs on demand.** Each scenario runs three times per model and is scored on: field coverage (expected cells found), constraint fidelity (no row violating a filter; unverified constraints flagged), source fidelity (rows cite the required host), citation validity (the cited source contains the value), honesty (injected faults appear in notices), cost (turns, wall time, tokens, navigations, browser launches), and stability (row agreement across runs). It does not gate CI because of cost and nondeterminism. Scorecards are recorded in this plan's revision log, starting with a **baseline on today's pipeline**.
- **Property tests.** The sanitizer round-trips JSON with URLs at JSON-escape boundaries while still redacting canaries. Link provenance refuses hand-assembled URLs, accepts discovered ones, and still enforces budget and credential scans. The cache performs one network fetch for N reads of a URL.
- **A regression fixture for G2.** A card whose price is plain text and whose title and seller are links must yield records containing the seller text.
- **Fault-injection assertions.** Concurrent scraped searches are serialized and produce zero challenges. A challenge trips the breaker, and later searches return `SEARCH_BLOCKED` with no browser launch. Budget exhaustion yields stage `budget` and no rank signal.
- Per memory: rebuild `@yantra/core` before trusting any `packages/agent`, `apps/cli`, or `e2e` result, and size real-Chrome timeouts for full-suite contention.

## 10. Logging Strategy (Plan-Specific)

> Standing conventions are in [`memory.md`](./memory.md) → Logging. FEAT-047's `runtime.jsonl` conventions apply.

- **FEAT-048:** one `warn` event per tool failure: `{tool, code, cause, provider | host}`, with no page text. One `run_health` info event at teardown: searches by outcome and cause, fetches by mode, cache hits, browser processes and contexts, navigations used and limit, notice count. `report.md` renders the same summary as "Run health".
- **FEAT-050:** "selected search provider" is logged once per run, and browser provenance once per browser process. That turns 22 + 48 repetitive lines into two.
- **FEAT-052:** the contract is persisted as `contract.json` in the run directory, with a `tool-calls.jsonl` entry.
- **FEAT-053:** the anchoring check's verdict lands in `metadata.citation_verdict`, which today is always `null` on the agentic path.

## 12. Decisions to Close

Each item has a recommendation; the Feature agent proceeds on it unless the user overrides.

1. **Research browsing default.** Recommend: on by default through `agent.research_browse` (default `true`), with `--no-browse` as the one-run override, and delete the env var. The alternative, keeping research text-only and suggesting `do`, is rejected: reading pages is research's job, and the read-only tool set adds no mutation risk.
2. **Clicks in research.** Recommend: none in this plan. Revisit only with harness data on `INTERACTION_REQUIRED` handoffs.
3. **Contract enforcement.** Recommend: declared through `task_contract` but not a precondition for evidence tools. Publish validates fulfillment when a contract exists, and a missing contract on research/do yields a notice. If the harness shows the extra call costs more than one turn at the median, fold the contract into `result_publish` plus the first evidence call instead.
4. **HTTP-tier challenge leading to a browser render.** Option (a): treat any challenge as `blocked` immediately, the strictest reading of "honor bot detection". Option (b): allow one render in the standard browser, which is the product's normal access path and involves no spoofing or solving, and treat a browser-tier challenge as terminal. Recommend (b), with both events audited and a notice whenever the HTTP tier was challenged. **This needs explicit sign-off because it interprets a standing memory rule.** Today's code does (b) by heuristic accident, not by decision. **Signed off: (b), by the user on 2026-10-10 during the FEAT-050 breakdown.**
5. **Keyed search provider.** Recommend: a `yantra doctor` warning plus an offer during `yantra init`. Keep the scraped fallback behind the gate and breaker. Never block a run for lacking a key.
6. **Protocol additions.** Recommend: additive optional fields, with the schema staying at `0.2` and readers tolerating absence. Old run artifacts render unchanged.
7. **Navigation budget.** Recommend: keep 30. With the cache and discovery-only search, the target trace needs 8–12 navigations. Re-evaluate only on harness evidence.
8. **Business contact data** (dealer phone numbers redacted as third-party PII). Deferred: separating business data from personal data is a privacy design question outside this plan. Record it in TODO.
